hypotheses.claim: FRANK's loop-of-loops architecture does not currently require a new first-class ClayCode loop primitive; existing record/state semantics plus the already-needed generic function/recursion-control closure can represent loop families when schedule/update policy is explicit data in typed IR.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: First-class loop semantics are required to statically enforce heterogeneous timescale, budget, intervention and rollback behavior without semantic leakage.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production ClayCode compiler/runtime counterexample where generic typed functions/state/control cannot preserve required loop behavior or safety while a first-class loop construct can.

hypotheses.claim: Executable loop scheduling policy belongs to ClayCode semantic identity: ORDERED_SEQUENTIAL schedules must retain order, while order normalization is only valid under explicitly order-independent synchronous snapshot/aggregation semantics.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Loop schedule can always be normalized as an unordered set because only loop membership matters.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched production traces showing all relevant sequential/coupled FRANK loop updates are order-independent under the admitted runtime semantics.

hypotheses.claim: Nested-loop calls need transitive type/effect closure, but effect expressibility must remain separate from external capability authority.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Per-function local effect declarations are sufficient and authority can be inferred from declared effect intent.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production compiler/runtime evidence that local-only summaries preserve all nested effects and do not permit hidden authority widening.

hypotheses.claim: The next BASE implementation step should prioritize production control-flow/type-effect/evaluator closure over new loop syntax.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A dedicated loop construct materially reduces implementation/repair cost or prevents safety failures that generic control-flow cannot.
hypotheses.falsifier: Executable production benchmark where first-class loop syntax yields a safety/semantic capability unavailable to generic typed control-flow rather than merely convenience.
